delta: 'Chapter two turns the sealing order from paper into a clock. In the vault Vance stops asking her
  brother to remember and asks his hands instead: put in front of the cradle, the graft hand finds the
  read-key seating sequence without him, and watching it he learns that the co-op took something out of
  him that he cannot name. The truth between the two of them moves from withheld to spoken, and the debt
  owed for the crushed hand is answered by the person who signed for it. In the gallery at the same hour
  the steward holds the order to its schedule. The shelf has moved the window forward, the only diver
  who can execute the order inside it is the one Quiej refused, and Quiej understands, without saying
  it to anybody, that the order will stand on the board and will not hold in fact. She chooses to let
  it fail slowly rather than to reopen it. Eight hours before either of those hours, Vance and Ilan are
  on the vault side of the throat with the door shut behind them, eleven metres from the Kestrel core,
  wanting a certainty about the seal ring that in this water can only be bought by touching it or by making
  a noise that says where you are. What Vance carries back out of that water she can defend. What it costs
  is kept in a separate account, and the account is her brother.'
